November, 1993    Page Reply

   PLEASE SEND YOUR TEXTFILE!
Text is accepted in any form for
OUTLETTERS: wordprocessor files
(say which),typed or handwritten
letters. However, PLEASE send us
a textfile if possible so your
letter needn't be typed again!
The easiest for us to edit are
Tasword 2 files with the right
margin set at 32 but a textfile
in ANY format is appreciated!

Please state if there should be
parts of your letter you do not
wish published but we always use
our discretion anyway. Letters
may also be edited for clarity
and length... Please ask if you
welcome direct correspondence
from other OUTLET readers and we
will publish your full address.

From Graham Yeardley, CAMBRIDGE


Dear Ron,

Just a quick question: RANDOMIZE
USR 0 resets the Spectrum but
leaves me in 48K mode. Is there
a similar command that will
reset to 128K mode other than
NEW and ERASE "M:"?

       Yours sincerely,

        Graham Yeardley

Brian Cavers to Graham Yeardley

No, the reset routine is in the
48K ROM. One way might be to
restore sysvars,clear variables,
delete BASIC, clear memory etc.
using a machine code routine in
screen memory which jumps to the
NEW command in the ROM to
finally clear the screen and go
to the 128K loader menu.

Another possibility from BASIC
might be POKE UDG and RASP sys-
vars to normal, CLEAR 65367,copy
A to S chars to the UDG area and
NEW which ought to normalize
everything! I assume the purpose
of your question IS to restore
all memory to normal -or why NOT
just use NEW?            - Brian


From J.A. Sharvell, HARROW


Dear Brian and Ron,

I am only using the Spectrum *3
because my grandson showed
little interest except for
games, which I suspect was 99%
of all owners.

Knowing nothing of computing, I
am amazed how few bits are
available at a reasonable price,
3.5" disc drives,mouse,printers,
memory upgrade. Your article
regarding PC's as you say,286 to
386 to 486 - 586,all upgradeable
and commonplace and mostly, as
far as I can see, compatible
with each other.


As an engineer I wonder what
happened to our whiz-kid
electronics experts that the
only extra I have found useful
is the Multiface 3,at reasonable
cost or perhaps I am expecting
too much from old equipment.

Although I've a few moans, this
winter I will persevere with it.
I'm too old to invest in a PC.

          Yours sincerely,

            J.A. Sharvell

Brian Cavers to J.A. Sharvell

In case anyone is misled I must
first clarify about upgrading
and compatibility of PC's. I
don't want people to think that
with all PC's you can just plug
in the latest processor and away
you go. I think with some you
can. I think I read that the 486
will readily upgrade to a 586
and I think the 386DX upgrades
reasonably to a 486 but I have
also seen adverts for a `200+
upgrade kit to convert from, I
think, a 286 to a 386. As you
can see I am a bit vague about
this field which is new to me.
What can be carried forward is
the monitor, keyboard, drives
etc. so you may simply need a
new main board.

The main point is that the PC
standard has such a huge base
that it looks set to last in
compatible upgradeability of
software for decades! Mind you,
I think there is a great deal of
hype about the increasing speed
and power - ALL of the software
we have seen this year has run
plenty fast enough on our 386.

As for the Spectrum, in its
day it has had a HUGE range of
add-ons, peripherals, plug-ins,
extras and so-on. It is simply
that you have probably arrived
at the sunset of the Spectrum's
day of glory. However, there is
still the long quiet evening to
enjoy.
                   - Brian

From Ron Smith, LONDON, N.9.

Dear Sirs, (Chris, Ron & Brian),

Again, well done! - for another
excellent edition (74), which
contained my boy Robert's AREA
FIND program. He was delighted
with your note and payment. It's
the thought that counts and
thanks again. He is working on
an upgraded version for the
whole of the UK STD numbers with
an internal compression program
so that it doesn't eat up all
the Speccy's memory. That will
be submitted at a later date.

Can the TABLOID program be
merged into one's own BASIC
programming efforts?
                      Ron Smith

Brian Cavers to Ron Smith


Thanks Ron.

No, as it is, TABLOID is so
integrated with our text decomp-
ressor that it would probably be
a bit messy to extract.

You could put a request in our
new OUTWORK section asking for a
TABLOID utility if you want then
if I or some other reader can
find time...

You need to specify clearly for
what you want to use it. Is it
for use with BASIC DATA or a
word processor text file. If a
text file, which format.


Our TABLOID is three columns of
32 characters each but one can
get three columns of 40 chars
with a couple of chars gap using
condensed mode.

The whole thing can actually be
done from BASIC quite easily but
rather slowly. The most puzzling
thing is how to calculate what
page goes where on the last
sheet. For example, if you have
three screen pages on the last
sheet they look odd vertically
and look more natural left to
right and yet when printed with
the full 9 pages on a full sheet
they DO go vertically! I had a
merry time working this out for
the SAM and then re-inventing it
for the PC version!


Just for interest,here's my est-
mate of where less than 9 blocks
of text should go on a sheet in
a 3 x 3 matrix...


   1          12          123


   134        135         135
   2          24          246


   147        147         147
   25         258         258
   36         36          369

Comments anyone?!! (like,"what's
he talking about?)

                         Brian

Graham Yeardley to G.L.R. Till


Dear Mr. Till,

I received a letter from Ron
Cavers of OUTLET saying that you
had written to them asking where
you might obtain a lead to conn-
ect a black-cased Amstrad monit-
or to a Spectrum that I wrote
about in my OUTLETTER in Issue
72.

The lead I have I obtained priv-
ately but have just phoned Need-
smore, a number supplied in an
earlier OUTLET and they said
that they have the lead in stock
priced `8.51. With V.A.T. and
postage it will cost `11.00.


Their address is...

     NEEDSMORE DISTRIBUTION
28, FARRIERS WAY INDUSTRIAL EST.
NETHERTON, MERSEYSIDE, L30 4XL
       TEL: 051 521 2202

The part number you require is
K2254. You might be able to get
it cheaper elsewhere but I found
these people very helpful,appar-
ently they stock something like
5,000 leads of various types.

I have no information on the pin
functions but hope this letter
will be of some use to you.

 [FOR FULL PIN CONNECTIONS SEE
  MALCOLM PERRY'S OUTLETTER IN
  THIS ISSUE! - Ed]


Dear Ron and Brian.

    Re:  Amstrad connector.

  [see also Graham Yeardley's
   reply to Mr. Till - Ed]

In reply to G.L.R. Till's quest-
ion,the connections on the 6-pin
plug on the colour monitor are
as follows: looking at the pin
end of plug they are numbered
anticlockwise from the gap and
pin 6 in the middle...

       PIN 1   RED
           2   GREEN
           3   BLUE
           4   H+V SYNC.
           5   EARTH
           6   not used


On the mono monitor they are...

       PIN 1   not used
           2    "   "
           3    "   "
           4   H+V SYNCS.
           5   EARTH
           6   COMP. VIDEO.

The +2a and +3 where the RGB
output is at "SCART" level and
the RGB output also incorporates
BRIGHT,a straightforward lead is
required and connect...

       Spectrum  to Monitor
          7           1
          6           2
          8           3
          4           4
          2           5


Remember, on the Spectrum 8 pin
connector numbering is in a non
logical order. i.e., from gap,
6,1,4,2,5,3,7 and 8 in middle.
This is looking at the socket on
the Spectrum and counting clock-
wise.

With the 128k and plus 2 the RGB
is at TTL level and BRIGHT is a
separate pin (pin 3). While dir-
ect connections do work to some
extent,to get the best it need a
bit of extra circuitry to reduce
RGB from 5V to 1V the monitor is
designed for and to obtain
BRIGHT this has been described
in past issues of OUTLET. I also
wonder if this method of obtain-
ing BRIGHT would work in answer
to F.Ridout on the CUB monitor?


The RGB monitor must be able to
respond and give different
levels of brightness with a
change of RGB level input. The
Amstrad does as it is a linear
monitor. a TTL monitor may not,
simply have ON or OFF RGB
response.

Before going to the trouble of
making up the circuit, a simple
test may give an indication:
Connect the neg, of a 1.5V cell
say AA or AAA type to monitor
earth. now connect one end of a
100 ohm resistor to pos. term
then touch other end to R input
(or G or B does not matter) and
note the brightness of that
colour.


Next repeat with two cells in
series (IE 3V) and see if the
brightness increases. If it does
then you can use the circuit
described to make the monitor
respond to BRIGHT.

I also have also found this
useful as a quick check to find
which is which for RGB inputs on
unknown monitor connections.
Remember TTL is nominal 5V so do
not exceed this voltage when
testing.

To obtain BRIGHT from +2 or 128k
involves connecting a resistor
in series with each of RGB
connections, 100ohm is typical .
now join the ANODES of three
diodes (1N914 or similar) to the
computer BRIGHT.

The cathode of each diode (the
end marked with a band) is then
connected to one side of 100 ohm
resistor. The other side of each
resistor then connects to RGB
and to the monitor end of each
of the resistors in the RGB
lines. Sync may need a series
resistor of about 1k ohn.

As I mentioned, a circuit on
these lines is already
incorporated in the +2A and +3
to give BRIGHT with the RGB.

4-core, individually-screened
lead is ideal for RGB+sync but
also find ribbon cable or even
ordinary multicore (with or
without overall screen) ok for
short lengths.


Now for something different...

Did you know you can have a
Disciple and +D on a Spectrum at
the same time? (without the need
for such as a Twoface)?

It came about that I wanted to
use a +D for a short time but
did not want the trouble of
unscrewing the Disciple. After
careful consideration I conclud-
ed it was unlikely plugging the
+D on to the back of the
Disciple would do actual damage,
at worst the system would simply
crash.

The interesting thing was that
with the Disciple inhibit button
OUT (Disciple enabled) entering
"RUN" - the Disciple boots.

With the button IN the +D boots;
you can have have both systems
booted: with button out the Dis-
ciple responds to disc commands,
with it in, the +D takes over.
It is because I presume the
Disciple ROM is in top half and
+D has it in the bottom half of
the system and why it does not
work with Unidos when both ROMs
are in the same area of memory.

While the discs seem OK and I've
not had any problems during the
many times this has been used
(however do not change system
during disc operations) SNAP
should be avoided as it is
unpredictable, most times SNAP
actually works but crashes on
return as I guess it gets confu-
sed as which it is to return to.

Printing also needs care;if only
one or the other is BOOTed then
a printer works in either case.
However, if both are booted at
the same time then only the
Disciple printer works - the +D
returns with an error report.

As I said I have used this many
times with no problems discwise
and put the idea forward in good
faith but it is up to individual
to decide if they wish to try it
and experiment for themselves .


       OUTLET PROMOTIONS.

I asked my local library if they
would accept an advert for
OUTLET, they replied "yes" on


the understanding that local
events must take priority on
space available. The notice may
have to be taken down from time
to time if space short and put
up again later. Still that is
better than nothing. No there is
no charge, even better!

So I knocked up a simply-worded
notice, decided to make it short
on the basis that people would
not bother to stand and read a
long, rambling,detailed page of
text. To make it stand out I
also did it in colour, "pinched"
bits of screens from Outlet and
Chezron adverts etc. I now had
an A5-size notice that while
pretty at close range could
easily get lost amongst host of
other posters.

I considered doing another in
A4-size but even so the quad-
size print mode is not really
large enough and the graphics
obtained from screens using
Stylewriter are still too small
for what I wanted.


I visited a local photocopy shop
and asked them how much it would
cost to blow up to A4 or bigger.
Quad printing doubled in size
nearer the mark, 25p in black
and white. So, why go to the
trouble of doing it in colour?

Or,how about a colour enlarge-
ment at nearly `2 a time (I will
not be having many of those).


Mind you, a colour ribbon only
does a few copies so is not
cheap and again must work out at
over `1 per printout. This is
mainly due to the way many
colour printing programs will
insist on printing yellow on top
of a stronger colour and so the
yellow track becomes "dirty" and
unusable after say half dozen
runs.

The LC10 itself is not totally
free from this "defect".The col-
our enlargement came out quite
well and looked better colour
and quality than the original .

So why not try your local libr-
ary and see what they say? They
may just say"yes,with pleasure"


There is something to be said
for the principle of "if you do
not ask (politely of course )
then they cannot say no". As an
example (nothing to do with
computing but out of interest).
If there is a big gap after this
the editor decided I rambled on
too much and cut it out.

Up until about the early 60s
holidays by train were a regular
occurrence then when I learnt to
drive, the car took over and I
have not been on a train since.
So for something different I
recently joined some friends on
a train journey into Wales for
no other reason than a day out
on a train (4 hours each way and
an hour at the other end to grab
lunch).

Now We all have an interest in
radio, electronics and communi-
cation in general so the train
radio link was of obvious
interest. This line was single
track and "passing the token" or
permission to proceed was
carried out via radio. (some
lines still physically hand over
a TOKEN from one driver to
another to prevents two trains
meeting head-on on the same
line!!.

At the station before we started
the passing engine driver was
collared and asked where the
control room was that they were
in communications with, "over
there" and pointed to a signal
box, and went on his way.


On joining the train we happened
to be near the front and when
the driver got on he poked his
head round the door and asked if
we would like to take it in
turns to ride in the cab.

We therefore had an extremely
informative journey on how the
present day systems were
operated, first hand insight in
the way the "token" was passed
in form of data and displayed on
a screen, not to mention a
friendly chat on things in
general about the history of the
line.

Now on return to the same
station the signal box was more
closely inspected and the one
colleague said...

"Well I can ask,he can only tell
me I should not be here.", and,
mounting the steps to the box,he
poked his head round the door
and said "I understand you con-
trol the whole line from here"..

No he was not told to clear off!
there followed an extremely int-
eresting explanation of the way
things operated,changes that had
been made and a new system about
to be tested on that line that
would let them pinpoint the
position of a train to within
less than a mile via satellite
(far better than "somewhere
within a 15-mile section of the
line" as now). Unfortunately the
discourse was cut short by the
arrival of our next train.


By the way, did you know some of
the level crossings in the quiet
country areas are operated by
the "high tec" method of the
train has to stop, the driver
leans out of the cab, pulls a
length of cord that is connected
to a switch and sets crossing
lights and barrier in operation?
At others, the guard has to get
out of train to press a button
and wait for the lights to
change - just like a pedestrian
crossing!

As I say if you do not ask.....
You will never know.. The simple
question at the start led on to
far more than ever expected.

                 Malcolm Perry
.

Brian Cavers to Malcolm Perry

Many thanks for all your efforts
promoting OUTLET, Malcolm!

Regarding that +D/Disciple joint
piggyback  - I wonder if two
Disciples might be joined?!! It
seems to me that the fact that
the +D and Disciple have their
ROMS in opposite halves of the
first 16K of memory should not
be relevant because each inter-
face has its own 8K of ROM and
8K of RAM.Still, what do I know?

Have you tried the OUT 31 soft
switch method? If that works
then you have effectively found
a method of having FOUR drives
on a Spectrum!
                     Brian

From Vision of The Mad Guys


As I'm relatively new to Outlet
I've got some questions and may
be you can help me:

1. When I write articles for you
can I send them to other fan-
zines too or shall they only be
published in Outlet?This is just
because I want to support some
other fanzines too.

2. Who does these fab title-
screens for you?

3. Is there still a software
publisher to whom I can send a
program which might be worth
selling (on Speccy)?


Okay, now some general comments
on the situation of the Speccy.
We had the same situation in
1988 when the last commercial
German mag for our Speccy
disappeared followed by software
and hardware sellers and so many
users bought new computers. I
didn't sell my Speccy but I
didn't work with it anymore.
This changed in 1990 when a new
mag called "Computer Flohmarkt"
appeared. It's like a mailbox on
paper where all computer users
(from all machines) can publish
small programs, do reviews, or
just exchange the newest infos.
Beside of this mag we have one
Spectrum and SAM club left with
about 170 members(Spectrum Profi
Club).


Now, why do I tell you this? I
think the same will happen in UK
too but there will always be a
group of users who will keep the
Speccy or SAM and support it.


The most important thing is in
my opinion to keep the people
informed what is happening and
that there still IS something
happening. A user who has no
contacts and no infos about what
is going on or where to get pro-
grams will probably buy another
computer.

But will there still be new pro-
grams or hardware stuff for the
Speccy? Yes!...


Concerning hardware,we have many
good developers in Germany (no
professionals indeed) who did
things like a Speccy running
with 10MHz (Three times as fast
as a normal Speccy) or new fast
I/O interfaces and there will be
some in UK too.

On the software side there is a
great PD and Demo market which
is the only future for Speccy I
think.Especially, demos impress-
ed many users and so they start-
ed to do programs by themselves.


In the UK this just begins to
wake up as some new demo groups
appeared lately.


So we only can  hope  bright  of
the future even if  there  won't
be that many users as there were
in the "big" times of Speccy.

Get into it!

       Vision of The Mad Guys

Brian Cavers to Vision

1. Yes, we claim no copyright in
contributed articles OR programs
- this remains with the author
unless he declares his work in
the public domain.So,they can be
sent elsewhere for publication
(of course, the later publishers
might grumble if they know of
its previous publication).

2. Most of our best recent title
screens are done by Dusan Balara
in Slovakia.He is also now doing
some great PC screens for us!One
or two other recent ones are by
us usually by taking existing PD
clip art images and composing,
editing and colouring them with
added material and text into the
final new screen.

3. Not really, the Spectrum com-
mercial software market, whether
games or utilities has totally
collapsed.The remnants could not
possibly continue without a maj-
or, nationally-distributed mag-
azine in which to promote their
products. We can sell games and
other programs ourselves separ-
ately from OUTLET with a royalty
to the author(usually about 40%)
but don't expect to sell them in
their thousands! Don't be dis-
appointed if they only sell a
few a month. However, such would
have a longer "shelf-life" than
most games sold in shops.

                     - Brian

From Fred Ridout, SWINDON

Dear Sir,

I would like to put a 3.5mm
socket in one of my +2's to use
an [external] tape-recorder, by
breaking the tape deck data out
lead. Do you think this would be
OK?

Thank you for advice on the
mouse - it reads OK now. All I
need to know is how to enter it
in a program.

Next I have a lead to connect
two +2's and FIDO128[OUTLET 44].
What happens next, ie,explaining
the menu etc and entering a pro-
gram.


If you are not too bored, one
more item. In BASIC programs you
put, eg, "GO TO CODE "NOT".Is it
done to save memory and how do
you get CHR$ below 32 (CODE"?").

I took the part of the program
that prints off the inflate pro-
gram for my own use as the lett-
ers are wonderful on a monitor.I
hope this is alright to do this?

Thank you for your tolerance and
terrific service.
                  Yours,

                     Fred

PS. I like the unselfish hope to
bolster the Spectrum tape OUTLET
with a PC OUTLET revenue!


Brian Cavers to Fred Ridout

It's possible to use an external
tape deck but I can't find any
info on this although I am sure
we had something in OUTLET in
the last year or so.

Can any other read help here to
find the previous reference or
to clarify how it's done? I am
trying to make an extra effort
to keep a mini-index of useful
hints from OUTLETTERS but it
does tend to get missed at this
busy time of the month!

I think the FIDO128 info was
aimed at users who already knew
of an earlier version. This is
what I think you do...


It is only intended for text or
code - not BASIC. If you select
MOVE file you can load a file.
If you then set the SAVE SESSION
to YES and then select TERMINAL
I think that sends it and the
user receiving sets SAVE SESSION
to NO and selects TERMINAL to
receive. I think parity needs to
be 8 bits. You may need to exp-
eriment a bit. However, there is
now a better program called
SPECTERM which I hope to put in
a future OUTLET. If you can't
wait, contact BG SERVICES (see
OUTBOARD) - it's only `1.50 for
their PD TAPE which contains
SPECTERM.

See last month's OUTLETTERS for
info on using the mouse.


Yes, the CODE and VAL functions
are used to save memory. The
Spectrum stores 6 extra hidden
bytes with every ordinary number
in BASIC to help speed it up and
using CODE or VAL saves this.

The original Spectrum manual has
a list of CODE words. If you do
not have it use FOR N= 32 TO 255
: PRINT N;" ";CHR$ N : NEXT N

The entire listing can be conv-
erted using OMNIVAC in Issue 28.
However, avoid VAL in parts of a
program where speed is important
as it is slower. OMNIVAC enters
the lower CODE numbers which you
cannot enter directly but higher
ones can be entered directly in
48K BASIC (precede with THEN for
command words then delete).

I have been unable to trace the
"inflate" program to which you
refer. Please give the true pro-
gram name and Issue and I will
let you know. However, it is
usually alright to cannabalise
our own programs for your own
use.

                   Brian.

From Graham Yeardley, CAMBRIDGE

Dear Ron,

Just a quick question: RANDOMIZE USR 0 resets the Spectrum but leaves me in 48K mode. Is there a similar command that will reset to 128K mode other than NEW and ERASE "M:"?

Yours sincerely,

Graham Yeardley

No, the reset routine is in the 48K ROM. One way might be to restore sysvars,clear variables, delete BASIC, clear memory etc. using a machine code routine in screen memory which jumps to the NEW command in the ROM to finally clear the screen and go to the 128K loader menu.

Yours sincerely,

J.A. Sharvell

In reply to G.L.R. Till's quest- ion,the connections on the 6-pin plug on the colour monitor are as follows: looking at the pin end of plug they are numbered anticlockwise from the gap and pin 6 in the middle...

PIN 1   RED 2   GREEN 3   BLUE 4   H+V SYNC. 5   EARTH 6   not used

On the mono monitor they are...

PIN 1   not used

```text
           2    "   "
           3    "   "
```

4   H+V SYNCS. 5   EARTH 6   COMP. VIDEO.

The +2a and +3 where the RGB output is at "SCART" level and the RGB output also incorporates BRIGHT,a straightforward lead is required and connect...

Spectrum  to Monitor

```text
          7           1
          6           2
          8           3
          4           4
          2           5
```

Remember, on the Spectrum 8 pin connector numbering is in a non logical order. i.e., from gap, 6,1,4,2,5,3,7 and 8 in middle. This is looking at the socket on the Spectrum and counting clock- wise.

With the 128k and plus 2 the RGB is at TTL level and BRIGHT is a separate pin (pin 3). While dir- ect connections do work to some extent,to get the best it need a bit of extra circuitry to reduce RGB from 5V to 1V the monitor is designed for and to obtain BRIGHT this has been described in past issues of OUTLET. I also wonder if this method of obtain- ing BRIGHT would work in answer to F.Ridout on the CUB monitor?

The RGB monitor must be able to respond and give different levels of brightness with a change of RGB level input. The Amstrad does as it is a linear monitor. a TTL monitor may not, simply have ON or OFF RGB response.

Before going to the trouble of making up the circuit, a simple test may give an indication: Connect the neg, of a 1.5V cell say AA or AAA type to monitor earth. now connect one end of a 100 ohm resistor to pos. term then touch other end to R input (or G or B does not matter) and note the brightness of that colour.

Next repeat with two cells in series (IE 3V) and see if the brightness increases. If it does then you can use the circuit described to make the monitor respond to BRIGHT.

I also have also found this useful as a quick check to find which is which for RGB inputs on unknown monitor connections. Remember TTL is nominal 5V so do not exceed this voltage when testing.

To obtain BRIGHT from +2 or 128k involves connecting a resistor in series with each of RGB connections, 100ohm is typical . now join the ANODES of three diodes (1N914 or similar) to the computer BRIGHT.

The cathode of each diode (the end marked with a band) is then connected to one side of 100 ohm resistor. The other side of each resistor then connects to RGB and to the monitor end of each of the resistors in the RGB lines. Sync may need a series resistor of about 1k ohn.

As I mentioned, a circuit on these lines is already incorporated in the +2A and +3 to give BRIGHT with the RGB.

4-core, individually-screened lead is ideal for RGB+sync but also find ribbon cable or even ordinary multicore (with or without overall screen) ok for short lengths.

Now for something different...

Did you know you can have a Disciple and +D on a Spectrum at the same time? (without the need for such as a Twoface)?

The interesting thing was that with the Disciple inhibit button OUT (Disciple enabled) entering "RUN" - the Disciple boots.

With the button IN the +D boots; you can have have both systems booted: with button out the Dis- ciple responds to disc commands, with it in, the +D takes over. OUTLET PROMOTIONS.

I asked my local library if they would accept an advert for OUTLET, they replied "yes" on

the understanding that local events must take priority on space available. The notice may have to be taken down from time to time if space short and put up again later. Still that is better than nothing. No there is no charge, even better!

I visited a local photocopy shop and asked them how much it would cost to blow up to A4 or bigger. Quad printing doubled in size nearer the mark, 25p in black and white. So, why go to the trouble of doing it in colour?

Or,how about a colour enlarge- ment at nearly `2 a time (I will not be having many of those).

Mind you, a colour ribbon only does a few copies so is not cheap and again must work out at over `1 per printout. This is mainly due to the way many colour printing programs will insist on printing yellow on top of a stronger colour and so the yellow track becomes "dirty" and unusable after say half dozen runs.

The LC10 itself is not totally free from this "defect".The col- our enlargement came out quite well and looked better colour and quality than the original .

So why not try your local libr- ary and see what they say? They may just say"yes,with pleasure"

There is something to be said for the principle of "if you do not ask (politely of course ) then they cannot say no". As an example (nothing to do with computing but out of interest). If there is a big gap after this the editor decided I rambled on too much and cut it out.

Up until about the early 60s holidays by train were a regular occurrence then when I learnt to drive, the car took over and I have not been on a train since. So for something different I recently joined some friends on a train journey into Wales for no other reason than a day out on a train (4 hours each way and an hour at the other end to grab lunch).

Now We all have an interest in radio, electronics and communi- cation in general so the train radio link was of obvious interest. This line was single track and "passing the token" or permission to proceed was carried out via radio. (some lines still physically hand over a TOKEN from one driver to another to prevents two trains meeting head-on on the same line!!.

At the station before we started the passing engine driver was collared and asked where the control room was that they were in communications with, "over there" and pointed to a signal box, and went on his way.

On joining the train we happened to be near the front and when the driver got on he poked his head round the door and asked if we would like to take it in turns to ride in the cab.

We therefore had an extremely informative journey on how the present day systems were operated, first hand insight in the way the "token" was passed in form of data and displayed on a screen, not to mention a friendly chat on things in general about the history of the line.

Now on return to the same station the signal box was more closely inspected and the one colleague said...

"Well I can ask,he can only tell me I should not be here.", and, mounting the steps to the box,he poked his head round the door and said "I understand you con- trol the whole line from here"..

No he was not told to clear off! there followed an extremely int- eresting explanation of the way things operated,changes that had been made and a new system about to be tested on that line that would let them pinpoint the position of a train to within less than a mile via satellite (far better than "somewhere within a 15-mile section of the line" as now). Unfortunately the discourse was cut short by the arrival of our next train.

By the way, did you know some of the level crossings in the quiet country areas are operated by the "high tec" method of the train has to stop, the driver leans out of the cab, pulls a length of cord that is connected to a switch and sets crossing lights and barrier in operation? At others, the guard has to get out of train to press a button and wait for the lights to change - just like a pedestrian crossing!

As I say if you do not ask..... You will never know.. The simple question at the start led on to far more than ever expected.

Malcolm Perry .

В моделях +2a и +3, где выход RGB имеет уровень "SCART", а также включает сигнал BRIGHT (яркость), требуется простой кабель, соединяющий...

          6           2
          8           3
          4           4
          2           5

Помните, что нумерация 8-контактного разъема на Spectrum нелогична, т.е. от разрыва: 6, 1, 4, 2, 5, 3, 7 и 8 в центре. Это если смотреть на разъем Spectrum по часовой стрелке.

В моделях 128k и Plus 2 RGB работает на уровне TTL, а BRIGHT — это отдельный контакт (контакт 3). Хотя прямые соединения работают до некоторой степени, для достижения наилучшего результата требуется небольшая дополнительная схема для снижения уровня RGB с 5В до 1В (на который рассчитан монитор), а также для получения сигнала BRIGHT; это описывалось в прошлых выпусках OUTLET. Интересно, сработает ли этот метод получения BRIGHT в ответ на вопрос F. Ridout о мониторе CUB?

RGB-монитор должен быть способен реагировать и выдавать разные уровни яркости при изменении входного уровня RGB. Монитор Amstrad может, так как он линейный. Монитор TTL может не уметь этого, просто имея реакцию ON/OFF для RGB.

Прежде чем браться за создание схемы, можно провести простой тест: соедините минус батарейки 1,5В (типа AA или AAA) с землей монитора. Теперь соедините один конец резистора 100 Ом с плюсом батарейки, затем коснитесь другим концом входа R (или G, или B, неважно) и заметьте яркость этого цвета.

Затем повторите с двумя батарейками последовательно (т.е. 3В) и посмотрите, увеличится ли яркость. Если да, то вы можете использовать описанную схему, чтобы заставить монитор реагировать на BRIGHT.

Я также нашел этот метод полезным в качестве быстрой проверки, чтобы определить, где какой вход RGB на мониторах с неизвестной распиновкой. Помните, что TTL — это номинальные 5В, поэтому не превышайте это напряжение при тестировании.

Для получения BRIGHT с +2 или 128k нужно подключить резистор последовательно с каждым из RGB-соединений, 100 Ом — типичное значение. Теперь соедините АНОДЫ трех диодов (1N914 или аналогичных) с контактом BRIGHT компьютера.

Катод каждого диода (конец, отмеченный полосой) подключается к одной стороне резистора 100 Ом. Другая сторона каждого резистора затем подключается к RGB и к концу соответствующих резисторов в линиях RGB со стороны монитора. Для синхронизации может потребоваться последовательный резистор около 1 кОм.

Как я уже упоминал, схема по этим принципам уже встроена в +2A и +3 для получения BRIGHT с RGB.

4-жильный кабель с индивидуальным экранированием идеально подходит для RGB+sync, но также можно использовать ленточный кабель или даже обычный многожильный (с общим экраном или без него) для коротких отрезков.

Знаете ли вы, что можно иметь Disciple и +D на Spectrum одновременно? (без необходимости использования чего-то вроде Twoface).

Это произошло потому, что мне нужно было использовать +D на короткое время, но я не хотел возиться с откручиванием Disciple. Тщательно всё обдумав, я пришел к выводу, что подключение +D к задней части Disciple вряд ли нанесет реальный ущерб, в худшем случае система просто зависнет.

Интересно то, что с нажатой кнопкой ингибитора (inhibit) Disciple (Disciple включен) при вводе "RUN" — Disciple загружается.

Когда кнопка НАЖАТА, загружается +D; можно загрузить обе системы: при отжатой кнопке на дисковые команды откликается Disciple, при нажатой управление перехватывает +D. Полагаю, это связано с тем, что ПЗУ Disciple находится в верхней половине, а у +D — в нижней половине системной памяти, и именно поэтому схема не работает с Unidos, когда оба ПЗУ находятся в одной и той же области памяти.

Хотя с дисками, похоже, всё в порядке, и за многократное использование у меня не возникло никаких проблем (впрочем, не переключайте системы во время дисковых операций), функции SNAP следует избегать — она непредсказуема; в большинстве случаев SNAP действительно срабатывает, но при возврате зависает, поскольку, как я догадываюсь, путается, куда именно возвращаться.

С печатью тоже нужна осторожность: если загружена только одна система, принтер работает в любом случае. Однако если загружены обе одновременно, работает только принтер Disciple — +D возвращает сообщение об ошибке.

Как я уже сказал, я пользовался этим много раз без каких-либо проблем с дисками и делюсь идеей из лучших побуждений, но каждый сам должен решать, хочет ли он попробовать и поэкспериментировать на свой страх и риск.

Все мы интересуемся радио, электроникой и связью вообще, поэтому поездная радиосвязь вызвала понятный интерес. Линия эта была однопутной, и «передача жезла», то есть разрешения на движение, осуществлялась по радио. (На некоторых линиях машинисты до сих пор физически передают друг другу ЖЕЗЛ из рук в руки, чтобы два поезда не столкнулись лоб в лоб на одном пути!).

На станции перед отправлением мы перехватили проходящего машиниста и спросили, где находится диспетчерская, с которой они держат связь. «Вон там», — указал он на стрелочный пост и пошёл своей дорогой.

Сев в поезд, мы случайно оказались в начале состава, и когда машинист вошёл, он заглянул в дверь и спросил, не хотим ли мы по очереди прокатиться в кабине.

Таким образом, мы провели чрезвычайно познавательную поездку, узнав, как работают современные системы, из первых рук увидели, как «жезл» передаётся в виде данных и отображается на экране, не говоря уже о дружеской беседе обо всём подряд из истории этой линии.

Вернувшись на ту же станцию, мы внимательнее осмотрели стрелочный пост, и один из коллег сказал:

«Ну, я хотя бы спрошу — максимум он скажет, что мне сюда нельзя». И, поднявшись по ступенькам к будке, он заглянул в дверь со словами: «Насколько я понимаю, отсюда управляется вся линия?»...

И нет, его не выставили вон! Последовал чрезвычайно интересный рассказ о том, как всё устроено, какие изменения произошли и о новой системе, которую собирались тестировать на этой линии, — она позволит определять местоположение поезда с точностью до мили с помощью спутника (куда лучше, чем нынешнее «где-то на 15-мильном участке пути»). К сожалению, беседу прервало прибытие нашего поезда обратно.

Кстати, знаете ли вы, что на некоторых железнодорожных переездах в глухих сельских районах применяется такой «высокотехнологичный» способ: поезд должен остановиться, машинист высовывается из кабины, дёргает за шнур, соединённый с выключателем, и запускает работу светофоров и шлагбаума? Информацию по использованию мыши смотрите в прошлом выпуске OUTLETTERS.

Да, функции CODE и VAL используются для экономии памяти. Spectrum сохраняет 6 дополнительных скрытых байтов с каждым обычным числом в BASIC для ускорения работы, а использование CODE или VAL позволяет их сэкономить.

В оригинальном руководстве к Spectrum есть список слов CODE. Если у вас его нет, используйте:

```text
FOR N= 32 TO 255 : PRINT N;" ";CHR$ N : NEXT N
```

Весь листинг можно преобразовать с помощью OMNIVAC из 28-го номера. Однако избегайте VAL в тех частях программы, где важна скорость, так как работает она медленнее. OMNIVAC вводит нижние коды CODE, которые вы не можете ввести напрямую, но более высокие можно ввести напрямую в 48K BASIC (вводите после THEN для командных слов, а затем удаляйте THEN).
